subject: chemistry
question_text: State and explain Graham's law of diffusion. Give its applications.

verification.note: Chapter 4 (States of Matter) is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.62-66), which prints the question, its star rank and a model answer. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. The book prints NO Long Answer section for this chapter, so no 8-mark form is invented. The mark splits are CLAIMS until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms them; both question lengths are sourced (the 2-mark form is the book's VSAQ 22, the 4-mark form is its three-star SAQ 1). SPELLING: the book prints the coal-mine application as ansil's alarm; the device is Ansell's alarm, a marsh-gas (methane) alarm that works on diffusion. The card uses the corrected name. The deduction of this law from the kinetic gas equation is a different question and is authored separately (SAQ 3). AI chemistry check 2026-08-25. Statement (RATE, inversely proportional to √d / √M, at constant T and P), the ratio form r₁/r₂ = √(M₂/M₁) = √(d₂/d₁) = √(VD₂/VD₁) and M = 2 × VD all verified; UF₆ isotope separation and Ansell's marsh-gas alarm are both correct applications. One memory_tip idiom ("ride on") replaced per Rule 41. No marked line changed.

steps.label: The statement
lines: Graham's law of diffusion: at constant
temperature and pressure, the rate of diffusion
of a gas is inversely proportional to the square
root of its density (or vapour density, or
steps.why: The law is a comparison, so its statement must fix the conditions (same temperature and pressure) and name the property the rate depends on — the square root of density or molar mass.
common_mistakes: Leaving out at constant temperature and pressure.
Saying proportional instead of INVERSELY proportional.
steps.memory_tip: Lighter diffuses faster — so the molar mass must sit under the rate, inside a square root.
steps.margin_note: The two conditions plus inversely proportional to the square root make the marked sentence.

steps.label: The expressions
lines: For two gases at the same T and P:
steps.why: The working form of the law is the two-gas ratio: the subscripts swap sides inside the root, and molecular weight can replace density because at the same T and P density is proportional to molar mass.
common_mistakes: Writing r₁/r₂ = √(M₁/M₂) — the subscripts must swap inside the root.
Forgetting M = 2 × VD when the data gives vapour density.
steps.memory_tip: Rate of 1 over rate of 2 equals root of M of 2 over M of 1 — always the OTHER gas's mass on top.
steps.margin_note: The ratio form is the one every numerical uses; write it even when not asked.

steps.label: Applications
lines: 1) Separation of isotopes — ²³⁵U is separated
from ²³⁸U by diffusing their volatile hexa-
fluorides (UF₆); the lighter one diffuses faster.
2) Ansell's alarm in coal mines — marsh gas
(methane) diffuses into the alarm faster than air
and its build-up sets off the warning.

lines.text: r₁/r₂ = √(M₂/M₁) at constant T and P

steps.why: Both applications work because a mass difference becomes a rate difference: the tiny mass gap between ²³⁵UF₆ and ²³⁸UF₆ separates isotopes over many diffusion stages, and light methane entering faster than air is what the mine alarm detects.
common_mistakes: Naming only one application when the question says applications.
Writing that uranium metal itself is diffused. The gas UF₆ diffuses, not the metal.
steps.memory_tip: One application separates (isotopes), one warns (the mine alarm) — both work because the lighter gas diffuses faster.
steps.margin_note: One mark per application; the boxed relation restates the law the applications use.
